accuracy.evidence: Every data set was recomputed with the Ar values on the AQA and OCR data sheets (H 1.0, C 12.0, N 14.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0, P 31.0, S 32.1, Fe 55.8): CH₂O 40.0/6.7/53.3 gives 1 : 2.01 : 1; Fe₂O₃ 69.9/30.1 gives 1 : 1.50; CH₃ 80/20 gives 1 : 3.00; NO₂ 30.4/69.6 gives 1 : 2.00; Na₂SO₄ 32.4/22.6/45.0 gives 2.00 : 1 : 3.99; C₃H₈ 81.8/18.2 gives 1 : 2.67; P₂O₅ 43.6/56.4 gives 1 : 2.51; C₂H₆O 52.2/13.0/34.8 gives 2 : 5.98 : 1; challenge answers CH₄, Fe₃O₄ (1 : 1.33), N₂O₅ (1 : 2.50), SO₃ (1 : 3.01), CH₂ and Al₂O₃. Built-formula percentages (Na₂SO₄ 32.4/22.6/45.0, C₂H₆O 52.2/13.0/34.8) match the data within 0.1. The familyTip's 35% N in NH₄NO₃ is 28/80. Parameterised answers a and 2*a+1 are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors named in RSC and exam-board examiner reports for empirical formula questions: mass ratio read as atom ratio (prediction 1, robot claim 1, m3, challenge 'mass'), dividing by the atomic number (chips 6, 8, 7, 15, 26, p1 hint, challenge 'z'), dividing oxygen by 32 for O₂ (32.0 and 28.0 chips, p2 and m1 hints, robot claim 3, challenge 'o2'), dividing by the largest (scene 2 feedback shows the sub-1 ratios), rounding 1.5, 2.5 or 1.33 (prediction 2, the ×1 lock-in message, p4, p5, m8, robot claims 4-5, challenge 'round' and 'tworound') and a ratio that still shares a factor (×4 lock-in message, the C₄H₁₂O₂ check in the build scene, m6, challenge 'notsimple').

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab runs this calculation's own pipeline: per-element chips for Ar versus atomic number or Mr of X₂, live gram and mole bars side by side, a tap-to-divide bar chart that shows the sub-1 ratios when the wrong amount is chosen, a 1-6 multiplier knob over dashed whole-number lines, and an atom-count builder that computes mass percentages from Ar and compares them with the data. flagformula (molecular, structural and displayed formulae) and the relative formula mass lab only draw or sum formulae; none turns percentages into a ratio. The lab_distinct gate keeps flag_empf.js under 30% similar to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each stage is discovered before it is stated: after dividing, the mole bar for oxygen comes out the same height as carbon's even though its mass bar is taller; tapping the H bar in the hydrocarbon shows C 0.33 : H 1.00; at ×1 the lock-in reports that rounding Fe 1 : O 1.5 to FeO₂ would give 63.6% Fe against the data's 69.9%; moving the knob turns bars green only on whole numbers; in the build scene the yours-versus-data bars only line up at Na₂SO₄ and C₂H₆O, and the learner sees a wrong guess like NaSO₄ give 19.3% Na.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'Compound X is 40.0% carbon and 53.3% oxygen. More O atoms than C atoms?' (tempting: yes, because there is more oxygen by mass; the mole bars come out equal, 3.33 each) and 'Fe : O is 1 : 1.50. What comes next?' (tempting: round to 1 : 2; the ×1 lock-in shows FeO₂ fails the percentage check and ×2 gives Fe₂O₃). Each step's completion message reveals the learner's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions, each with two wrong answers built from a real slip (C₃H and S₂O₃ from the mass ratio, CH₂ from atomic numbers, N₄O₅ from dividing O by 32, FeO, NO₃ and AlO₂ from rounding, Fe₂O₃ from ×2 on 1.33, S₂O₆, C₂H₄ and Al₄O₆ from not simplifying). EMPF.SLIP holds seven distinct messages that name the slip and the fix, and the lab scenes add their own: atomic number versus Ar, Mr of the molecule versus single atoms, dividing by a non-smallest amount, rounding a fraction and a ratio that shares a factor.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text reads at FK 4.6 and the adult text at 7.8, under the 7.0 and 10.0 limits; sentences are short and each technical word (empirical formula, Ar, moles) is used with its meaning. Canvas numbers are dark on white cards over a pale blue bench, chip values show Ar to 1 d.p. and atomic numbers as whole numbers so the two are easy to tell apart, and the data and yours labels sit on two lines so they never collide at 390 px.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs cover: what an empirical formula is with glucose, why mass is not atom count with the 16× O to H example, the 100 g and divide-by-Ar-then-smallest method, and when to multiply versus round plus the percentage check. Adult paragraphs give the specification references and key words, the method with the advice to keep 3 s.f., five named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler and under 12% overlap with every other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light themes and desktop dark at every step, at rest and part-way through Show me, plus a mid-build state: three element columns with chips stacked vertically fit at 390 px, the bar charts keep labels inside their columns, the multiplier track spans the width with ×1-×6 labels readable and a 26 px knob, and the build scene's arrows are full-column tap targets. The buttons under the canvas wrap into rows of 44 px targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: one per chip ('C ÷ 12.0', aria 'Divide the C mass by 12.0'), '÷ C amount' per bar, '× smaller', '× bigger' and 'Lock in', '+1' and '−1' per element, Right and Slip. Results and every multiplier change are written to the canvas aria-label and spoken through c.say; challenge feedback is a polite live region. Matching is shown by text (percentages, 'yours' and 'data') as well as green. The walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
